overview: Hungary is a landlocked country in Central Europe. Its capital, Budapest, was formed in 1873 when the towns of Buda and Pest, on opposite banks of the Danube, were joined together. Hungarian is not related to most other European languages; its closest relatives include Finnish and Estonian. Hungary joined NATO in 1999 and the European Union in 2004.

geography.text: Much of Hungary is low, flat land in the Pannonian Basin, with the Great Hungarian Plain in the east. The Danube and the Tisza are its main rivers. In the west lies Lake Balaton, the largest lake in Central Europe. Hills rise in the north, but even the highest point is only just over 1,000 metres.
